tourism.detail: The Turkish MFA lists Australian ordinary passports as visa-exempt for touristic visits and transit up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
tourism.next: Do not assume the tourism exemption covers local work or paid speaking.

meetings.route: Business purpose to be confirmed with the Turkish mission
meetings.detail: The published Australian exemption is worded for touristic visits and transit; meetings, negotiations and trade activities need a purpose-specific check.
meetings.next: Ask the host/mission whether the planned meetings fit visa-free entry or require a visa.

conference.detail: An attendee may be a visitor; exhibitor, speaker, trainer or contractor may need a separate route.
conference.next: Get an invitation that names the exact programme role.

unpaid-speaking.detail: Unpaid lectures, panels and cultural exchange are not automatically covered by tourism entry; duties and host matter.
unpaid-speaking.next: Send the full invitation and no-fee/expense arrangement to the Turkish mission.
unpaid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

paid-speaking.route: Turkish work permit and work visa
paid-speaking.detail: Paid speaking, consulting, teaching and employment generally need a work permit coordinated with a Turkish employer or host.
paid-speaking.next: Have the employer/promoter begin the work-permit process before travel.
paid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

book-launch.route: Visitor for rights; work/cultural route for launch delivery
book-launch.detail: Rights meetings may be business-related, while paid readings, signings, workshops, local sales and merchandise need accurate Turkish treatment.
book-launch.next: Separate author appearance, rights, royalties and retail.
book-launch.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

ai-teaching.detail: Academic exchange and commercial AI teaching have different host and work requirements.
ai-teaching.next: Ask the institution to state appointment, pay and duration.
ai-teaching.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

remote-work.route: No broad dedicated Turkish digital-nomad visa located
remote-work.detail: Türkiye provides residence permits but no simple all-purpose remote-worker route in the official sources used here; foreign work, tax and local clients need confirmation.
remote-work.next: Confirm the residence basis and avoid local Turkish work on visitor entry.
remote-work.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

entrepreneur.detail: Forming or investing in a Turkish company does not by itself authorise personal work; operating status and permits are separate.
entrepreneur.next: Choose investor, company and work roles with Invest in Türkiye and the migration authority.
entrepreneur.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

trade.detail: Trade fairs, negotiations and sourcing may fit a business route, but the touristic exemption wording should not be stretched to active trade delivery.
trade.next: Ask the Turkish host to confirm business entry and customs/sales obligations.
trade.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

artist.route: Cultural work permit or host-led event route
artist.detail: Performance, filming, exhibition and music work need promoter and work-permit classification.
artist.next: State venue, producer, fee, royalties, crew and dates.
artist.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

mixed-mission.detail: Türkiye is a fast exploratory arrival, while speaking, teaching, trade and performance are host-led activation questions.
mixed-mission.next: Split tourism, meetings, remote work and local delivery before booking.
mixed-mission.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

laws.rule: Penalties for using or possessing drugs are severe. They include long jail sentences.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Mount Ararat (Ağrı Dağı), between the eastern provinces of Ağrı and Iğdır, is designated a 'special military zone'. You must hire the services of a locally licensed guide if you intend to hike in the area. A licensed company will obtain the necessary permits and assign you to a registered Mountaineer to accompany you throughout your hike. Visiting Mount Ararat (Ağrı Dağı), without the Turkish government's permission is an offence that could incur severe penalties.
laws.heading: Hiking Mount Ararat (Ağrı Dağı)

laws.rule: By law, you must always carry a photo ID. Police conduct random checks regularly. Turkish authorities do not accept Australian driver's licences as ID. Carry your passport with you at all times. Illegal activities could result in severe penalties, including: taking photos of military installations or prisons searching for historical artefacts without authorisation defacing or destroying Turkish currency failing to comply with Turkish visa conditions or immigration regulations supporting terrorist organisations, including expressions of support on social media It's illegal to 'insult': the Turkish flag the Turkish President or Government the founder of Türkiye, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk This incl
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: The Islamic holiday month of Ramadan is observed. Respect religious and cultural customs and laws at this time. During Ramadan, eating, drinking and smoking in public during the day may not be culturally appropriate in some areas. If you're not fasting, don’t eat, drink or smoke around people who are. Some areas are more tolerant of travellers and locals who don't fast. Seek local advice so you don’t offend. Explore our Ramadan page to learn more, including dates for Ramadan.
laws.heading: Ramadan

laws.rule: Same-sex consensual sexual activity between adults in private isn't a crime under Turkish law. But same-sex relationships aren't widely accepted in Turkish society especially outside of the large cities, and Türkiye doesn't legally recognise same-sex marriages, civil unions, or domestic partnerships. Avoid public displays of affection. This applies to everyone, regardless of your relationship status or sexual orientation. LGBTQIA+ events and gatherings have been subject to regular local government bans, including Pride Week. Turkish authorities have arrested LGBTQIA+ activists and protestors and members of the LGBTQIA+ community. Legal protections are limited.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ information

laws.rule: You can drive for up to 6 months if you have a valid Australian driver's licence (digital driver's licences may not be accepted). You must get a Turkish driver's licence, an International Driving Permit (IDP) or a notarised Turkish translation of your Australian licence if you plan to drive for longer than 6 months after your arrival. Authorities conduct random checks regularly.
laws.heading: Driving permit

laws.rule: Anyone bringing a drone into Turkey must apply for a technical conformity letter from SHGM, with identity details for a security check of the importer and end user.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Standards of dress and behaviour are conservative in many parts of Türkiye. Some regions are more conservative than others. Avoid offending locals by respecting religious and social traditions. Dress modestly, particularly at mosques and religious shrines. Avoid public displays of affection. This applies to everyone, regardless of your relationship status or sexual orientation. If in doubt, seek local advice. Presidency of Religious Affairs (Diyanet) mosque-visit rules: take off your shoes, cover shoulders and knees, women cover their hair, and don't photograph people praying. Visitors are closed out during prayer times.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: SHGM requires anyone importing a drone to apply for a technical conformity letter, with identity documents for a security check. Flights of drones between 4 kg and 150 kg need a flight permit. The commercial operator authorisation and foreign-pilot rules were not found.

items.text: Not yet checked: any public SHGM directory of drone operators.

SHGM's flight-permit page lists flights of unmanned aerial vehicles between 4 kg and 150 kg as needing a permit. The registration mark for drones starts with the letter 'I'; the registry page read is old. The commercial operator authorisation (SHT-IHA) was not read.

Anyone importing a drone into Turkey applies for a technical conformity letter; the application includes identity details for a security investigation of the importer and end user. Whether a foreign visitor can fly under another route was not found.
